prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for the conception and demonstration of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional PROTAC molecules

statement.case_for: Base editing (B024) is a clearly attributable, mechanistically transparent piece of chemistry: a deaminase is coupled to a catalytically impaired Cas protein so that a defined nucleotide is converted without a double-strand break. It has independent confirmation, clinical entry, and a decisive originator in Liu. PROTACs (B009) introduced a genuinely new modality, induced proximity to recruit an E3 ligase and remove a protein rather than inhibit it, with a measurable ternary-complex mechanism, strong independent confirmation and a clean founding paper (Sakamoto, Kim, Crews, Deshaies 2001). These are the two candidacies with the broadest opening support (six of eight members rank each), and together they give a coherent chemical-biology prize that fits the three-person limit if each part is kept compact.
statement.case_against: The weakest point is attribution under the three-person cap. Crediting Liu alone for B024 leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, whom several colleagues name, and crediting Crews and Deshaies alone for B009 omits Handa and Ito (cereblon and the molecular-glue lineage), Ciulli and Gray. Base editing may also be read as a follow-on to the 2020 genome-editing prize, and no PROTAC is yet an approved drug, so clinical proof is incomplete. My own opening first choice, nitrogenase (B038), is the kind of structure-plus-kinetics mechanism I value most, but it drew no support from any colleague and its attribution across Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe is hard to resolve, so I do not insist on it.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks PROTACs first as a simple chemical idea (induced proximity) with demonstrated consequences, and would credit Liu alone for base editing as the clean framing.
responses.response: I agree that Liu alone is the cleanest attribution for B024 and I have moved toward it from my opening trio. I qualify the PROTAC side: you propose Crews, Deshaies and Handa, but Handa's cereblon work is the molecular-glue lineage and is mechanistically separate from the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept. Putting both in one citation risks a prize that merges two histories. Keeping the citation on PROTACs and naming Crews and Deshaies is more defensible on priority, and the expert reports should settle whether the glue lineage deserves its own treatment.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling first as molecule-making at its core, widely used and overdue, but ranks PROTACs seventh because much of the mechanism is biology rather than chemistry.
responses.response: I share your high view of B003 and ranked it third, and I keep it as my first alternative. But on PROTACs I disagree with the chemistry-versus-biology objection: the novel element is the rational design of a heterobifunctional small molecule and its ternary-complex energetics, which is chemistry acting on a biological pathway. The real weakness of B003 is the one I raised in my opening: the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi and Migita precursors make it look incremental to some members, so I would not place it ahead of two candidacies with cleaner novelty.

responses.point: Sparr ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first for their physical-chemical principle and enormous clinical impact, and ranks base editing third with Liu alone.
responses.response: I recognize the pKa-tuned lipid mechanism and the clinical scale, and I did not rank B013 highly. My reservation is attribution and overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification: credit is spread over Vancouver, Inex and MIT groups and cannot be cleanly cut to three. We also agree that Liu alone is the clearest B024 attribution, which helps that part of any configuration.

responses.point: Linke ranks base editing first and PROTACs second, proposing Liu-Komor-Gaudelli for B024, and finds phase separation interpretively unsettled as a maturity issue.
responses.response: I accept your maturity point on B047, which I ranked seventh for the same reason. On B024, I understand the Liu-Komor-Gaudelli trio because Komor and Gaudelli wrote the two foundational papers. But if base editing shares a prize with PROTACs, the total of six names cannot stand, so a trio for B024 would force a single-achievement prize, which I think under-uses the strong B009 candidacy.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports support Liu alone, or a broader group, for base editing given Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida.
Whether the molecular-glue lineage (Handa, Ito) should be inside the PROTAC citation or treated separately.
Whether the committee regards base editing as a distinct chemical advance rather than an extension of the 2020 prize.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes B009 premature.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the preferred candidates. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, but her leading candidacies (dye-sensitized and perovskite solar cells) are not part of my preferred configuration.
